correctness.rationale: Full chain covariance identity reconstructed from the Markov eigenvalue, including negative memory; positivity of observed means permits normalization; inversion and backward model construction prove injectivity and exact feasibility. Two distinct rational models share every two-season observed cell; zero memory has a continuum of identical full laws; a distinct false-positive model shares six moments. The exact enumeration executable confirms these finite boundary instances. General claims rest on the analytic proof, not empirical enumeration.

value.rationale: Repeated within-season visits are costly or infeasible in species occupancy surveys. A sharp exactly-three-season population-moment design permitting completely unrestricted detection shifts is a motivated structural result, with an exact model-check equality, an identifiability boundary at zero turnover memory, and explicit local sensitivity. These facts directly clarify which low-order cross-season information substitutes for within-season replication and when it fails; no empirical precision or general HMM identifiability is claimed.
